children: Treasury yields ease slightly but remain elevated amid interest-rate anxiety. Several Fed officials speak today, following recent hawkish comments. President Trump and China's Xi will likely discuss trade. Oil prices rise 2%. U.S. weekly jobless claims slip to 197,000 from an upwardly revised 198,000, versus WSJ consensus forecast of 201,000. August new residential sales, due at 10 a.m. ET, are forecast to expand by 1.8%, after July's 10.5% decline. Yields move little on the jobs data. The 10-year is at 5.116%, down from a 19-year high of 5.149% reached overnight. The two-year slips to 4.862% from a overnight high of 4.907%. (paulo.trevisani@wsj.com; @ptrevisani)
